A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Stronger Normalization-Free Transformers, with matching authors, methods, and experiments. All 22 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original function-property experiments, function searches, multimodal model evaluations, and ablations, including additional results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds measured operator runtimes in Appendix F, Figure 13, and Table 27.

M1.justification: Derf retains the same erf-based operator, learnable scalar scale and shift, per-channel affine parameters, and normalization-replacement procedure. Formula clarifications and the newly documented Triton implementations do not establish a change to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-1K, LibriSpeech, GRCh38 with GenomicBenchmarks, and OpenWebText for the same tasks. The new runtime sweep varies operator hidden dimension without adding a dataset, application domain, or distinct task scenario.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain their function candidates and comparison methods, including LayerNorm, DyT, RMSNorm, and GroupNorm where previously evaluated. Appendix F reuses LayerNorm and DyT for timing comparisons; the newly cited related works are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix F introduces single-operator forward and backward timing across hidden dimensions, controlling batch size, sequence length, precision, fusion, and memory-access comparability. Existing training and evaluation protocols remain unchanged. Table 21's added initialization grids document previously described tuning rather than establish a revised protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds an analysis of computational cost and its dependence on hidden dimension, examining Derf relative to DyT and LayerNorm. Existing function-property analyses, shift ablations, approximation experiments, and fitting-versus-generalization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The added runtime results likewise provide no uncertainty estimates or repetition counts.

E6.justification: Table 3 changes unmodified arctan accuracy from 82.4% to 82.3% and isru from 82.3% to 82.2%. Appendix F adds runtime results: Table 27 reports forward/backward times of 0.42/0.73 ms for both Derf and DyT versus 0.42/0.74 ms for LayerNorm at 15k hidden dimension. Other task-performance results are retained.

T1.justification: Figure 3 revises the stated power23(x) definition from x^(2/3) to sign(x) times x^(2/3), correcting its extension to negative inputs consistently with the odd-function construction discussed elsewhere. The remaining mathematical framework is retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: Section 1 removes RMSNorm from its claim that Derf consistently surpasses the listed methods across all evaluated settings. This is a limited narrowing: the abstract still claims broad advantages over RMSNorm, and the central function-design contributions and conclusion remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix F links Derf's backward-runtime advantage at larger dimensions to increasing reduction and synchronization overhead in normalization layers, while acknowledging possible slower execution at small dimensions. The original explanation based on improved generalization and relative fitting capacity is retained.

D1.justification: Table 21 newly specifies GPT-2 alpha-initialization grids: {0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0} for attention-associated layers and {0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 1.0} for other layers. Appendix F discloses custom Triton kernels and timing controls, but omits hardware and exact batch/sequence sizes. The code-access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 8 adds bounded convolutional operators to its discussion, citing Deep Hyperspherical Learning (2017) and Decoupled Networks (2018). Research positioning otherwise remains stable. Consolidation of the duplicate stochastic-depth references does not remove a distinct cited work.

P1.justification: Changes include localized caption and prose edits, expansion of the NYU affiliation, reference cleanup, and the new Appendix F. The main section order, narrative, and existing appendix content remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 13 and Table 27, expands Table 21 with two initialization rows, and corrects the channel/token labels and explanation in Figure 1. Appendix material reflows, including relocation of Table 25, without removing existing displays.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves reproducibility by specifying initialization grids, corrects Figure 1's normalization-axis explanation, and adds useful computational-cost evidence absent from v1. The central method and empirical support remain stable. Missing hardware, exact input sizes, and uncertainty reporting limit the strength of the new timing evidence, so the overall improvement is incremental.
